title: Rooting Out Fraud or Election Scheming? DOGE Accused of Misusing Social Security Data

conservative.headline: DOGE Fighting Fraud: Media Hysteria Can't Hide Billions in Government Waste
conservative.byline: As seen on Fox News, Newsmax, Washington Examiner
paragraphs: While Democrats and the media manufacture outrage, DOGE is doing exactly what it was created to do: identify waste, fraud, and abuse in bloated government agencies.

White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt set the record straight on Fox News' 'Hannity,' explaining DOGE's mission at the Social Security Administration: "Number one, to identify duplicate payments and to end them. Number two, to identify payments that are going to deceased people who are no longer living. And number three, to protect the integrity of the system for hard working Americans who have been paying into it their entire lives."

Leavitt pushed back hard against media fearmongering: "So rest assured to all of the people watching your show tonight, if you paid into the system, honestly, you will continue to receive your Social Security checks. Do not buy into the lies from the legacy fake news media, who are trying to fear you and scare you into believing otherwise."

The Washington Examiner reported that the Justice Department's court filing actually shows SSA officials believed DOGE needed access to agency records to root out waste, fraud, and abuse—exactly what DOGE was created for.
Even Republican Sen. Chuck Grassley, chairman of the Senate Finance subcommittee on Social Security, told NBC News he had not been told ahead of time about DOGE's moves at the agency.

Acting SSA Commissioner Lee Dudek told Fox Business that "DOGE personnel CANNOT make changes to agency systems, benefit payments, or other information. They only have READ access." And SSA's own court filing confirmed that no Social Security data was ultimately shared with the outside advocacy group.
The real scandal isn't DOGE looking for fraud—it's that Washington has tolerated billions in waste for so long that actually trying to fix it sends the establishment into panic mode.

liberal.headline: Largest Data Breach in History: DOGE Caught Sharing Americans' Social Security Data with Election Deniers
liberal.byline: As seen on MSNBC, The New Republic, HuffPost, The Hill
paragraphs: The Trump administration has admitted in court filings that Elon Musk's DOGE team may have illegally shared the Social Security data of hundreds of millions of Americans with a political advocacy group seeking to overturn election results.

The New Republic's headline captured the scandal: "DOGE Goons May Have Used Social Security Data for Election Plot." According to DOJ court filings, a political advocacy group contacted DOGE employees with a request to analyze state voter rolls, with the stated aim "to find evidence of voter fraud and to overturn election results in certain States."

House Democrats Rep. John Larson and Richard Neal called it potentially "the largest data breach in our nation's history" and demanded a full criminal investigation. The lawmakers stated: "Elon Musk and his 'DOGE' believe they are above the law and refused to appear before Congress. Republicans have blocked every effort to hold this Administration accountable, voting down our resolutions demanding documents, even changing House Rules to shield 'DOGE' from accountability."

Sen. Elizabeth Warren was scathing: "The Trump-Musk Social Security takeover has only meant more chaos and confusion for Americans. Every one of DOGE's so-called 'mistakes' is a backdoor cut to people's benefits. There's nothing efficient about making it harder for people to access the checks they've earned and are owed."

AARP demanded accountability. Chief Advocacy Officer Nancy LeaMond stated: "SSA is entrusted with the sensitive data of hundreds of millions of Americans, and protecting that data from illegal use must be a top priority. Anyone involved must be held accountable and the Social Security Administration must take immediate steps to ensure nothing like this can happen again."

The court filings reveal DOGE employees used Cloudflare—an unauthorized third-party server—to share SSA data, and one employee signed a 'Voter Data Agreement' with an unnamed political advocacy group without any oversight from agency officials.

Warren noted the fraud claims were bogus from the start: DOGE claimed 40% of calls to SSA were fraudulent, but after implementing anti-fraud checks, SSA found only two cases out of over 110,000 that had a high probability of being fraudulent.

This isn't about finding fraud—it's about using the personal data of 300 million Americans to help election deniers overturn democracy. And Republicans are blocking every attempt to hold them accountable.

factcheck.headline: What Actually Happened with DOGE and Social Security Data
paragraphs: Both sides are spinning hard on this story. Here's what we actually know from the court filings—and what remains unclear.
THE UNDISPUTED FACTS:

✓ DOJ admitted data mishandling: In a January 2026 court filing, the Justice Department acknowledged that DOGE employees at SSA may have misused data, including sharing information through unauthorized Cloudflare servers and communicating with an outside advocacy group.

✓ An advocacy group sought voter roll matching: Court documents state a political advocacy group contacted DOGE employees "with a request to analyze state voter rolls" with the aim "to find evidence of voter fraud and to overturn election results in certain States."
✓ A 'Voter Data Agreement' was signed: One DOGE employee signed an agreement with the unnamed advocacy group in March 2025, without SSA officials' knowledge or approval.

✓ Two DOGE staffers referred for Hatch Act violations: SSA referred two DOGE employees to DOJ for potential violations of the Hatch Act, which prohibits using government positions for political purposes.

✓ Data was shared on unauthorized servers: DOGE team members used Cloudflare to share SSA data, violating agency security protocols. Personal information on approximately 1,000 individuals was sent via encrypted email to a DOGE associate.
CONSERVATIVE SPIN VS. REALITY:

⚠️ Claim: DOGE only has "READ access" and can't change anything — While technically true for benefit payments, the court filings show DOGE employees could and did export data to unauthorized external servers. Read access doesn't prevent data from being copied and shared.

⚠️ Claim: "No data was ultimately shared with outside groups" — SSA says it hasn't found evidence data was shared, but emails "suggest that DOGE Team members could have been asked to assist the advocacy group by accessing SSA data to match to voter rolls." The investigation is ongoing.

✓ Fair Point: DOGE's stated mission—finding waste, fraud, and abuse—is legitimate. Government efficiency reviews are normal. The question is whether DOGE pursued that mission properly or veered into political activity.
LIBERAL SPIN VS. REALITY:

⚠️ Claim: "Largest data breach in history" — This is hyperbole. While concerning, no mass data leak has been confirmed. The known incidents involve approximately 1,000 individuals' data shared via email and data stored on unauthorized servers. Serious, but not comparable to breaches affecting tens of millions.

⚠️ Claim: DOGE definitively "lied" about fraud — DOGE's 40% fraud claim was misleading—they confused "40% of fraud comes from phone calls" with "40% of calls are fraudulent." That's a significant error, but calling it a deliberate "lie" versus incompetence isn't proven.

✓ Fair Point: The court filings do show DOGE employees communicated with a group seeking to overturn elections and signed agreements without oversight. That's genuinely alarming regardless of whether data was ultimately shared.
WHAT WE DON'T KNOW:

• Who is the unnamed "political advocacy group"?
• Was Social Security data actually shared with them?
• What specific evidence led to the Hatch Act referrals?
• Why were DOGE employees communicating with election-denial groups?
• Will DOJ pursue criminal charges?

The Bottom Line: The court filings are genuinely damning—DOGE employees signed secret agreements with election-denial groups and used unauthorized servers to share government data. Whether this amounts to the "largest data breach in history" or incompetent process violations will depend on facts still emerging. What's clear is that DOGE operated with minimal oversight and may have crossed legal and ethical lines.
